papers.title: Optical Access to a Molecular Nuclear-Spin Register in Catalytically Relevant Palladium(I) Complexes
papers.authors: Sojung F. Kim, Erica Sutcliffe, Ryan G. Hadt
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Circularly polarized light generates electron-spin coherence in palladium complexes in solution. Time-resolved optical measurements resolve coupling to ligand phosphorus nuclei at ambient temperature, and pulsed EPR benchmarks the coherence. The same optical approach detects coherent dynamics in reaction mixtures.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Directly connects a chemically reactive molecular complex with optical access to an electron–nuclear spin system.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate molecular spin coherence in room-temperature solution.

papers.title: Magneto-Optical Studies on the Orbital Angular Momenta and Spin–Orbit Coupling in the Excited Triplet States of Octahedral Mo6 Clusters: Magnetic Circular Dichroism and Magnetic Circularly Polarized Luminescence
papers.authors: Hirohisa Yanagikawa, Toranosuke Tomikawa, Yuichi Kitagawa, Yasuchika Hasegawa, Kaplan Kirakci, Kamil Lang, Kazuyuki Ishii
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Magnetic circular dichroism and polarized luminescence probe excited triplet states in molybdenum clusters. Calculations connect the measured optical signals to orbital angular momentum, spin–orbit coupling and relaxation of the excited-state geometry.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides spectroscopic observables for assigning spin–orbit interactions in optically active molecular clusters.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine optical transitions and excited-state processes relevant to molecular spin interfaces.

papers.title: Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
papers.authors: Adarsh P. Raghuram, Francesca M. Blondell, Jonathan M. Mortlock, Benjamin P. Maddox, Sohail Dasgupta, Holly A. J. Middleton-Spencer, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Hannah M. Price, Philip D. Gregory, Simon L. Cornish
papers.summary: Microwave coupling among rotational states of ultracold rubidium–cesium molecules realizes a synthetic lattice. State-resolved measurements track its dynamics and test whether edge states survive perturbations that preserve or break the protecting symmetry.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Demonstrates coherent control and readout across several molecular levels over extended evolution times.

relatedPapers.reason: Both require selective addressing and coherent manipulation of molecular quantum states.

papers.title: Dynamical Decoupling using Universal Optimal Tracking
papers.authors: Amit Devra, Emanuel Malvetti, Niklas J. Glaser, Abhishek Agarwal, Ivan Rungger, Santana Lujan, Max Werninghaus, Stefan Filipp, Léo Van Damme, Steffen J. Glaser
papers.summary: An optimization method tracks qubit evolution at several waypoints to design decoupling sequences that compensate accumulating errors. Superconducting-qubit experiments test static control imperfections, while simulations examine the effect of time-dependent noise.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A control-design strategy that explicitly tests whether errors accumulate during repeated refocusing.

relatedPapers.reason: Both develop decoupling sequences intended to remain robust over repeated operations.

papers.title: Enhanced coherence of rare-earth nuclear spins in a crystal
papers.authors: Bassam Nima, Yuiki Takahashi, Amar Vutha
papers.versionEvidence: Matching title and author list in publisher metadata and arXiv record
papers.summary: Driving nuclear spins in the host crystal extends the coherence of europium nuclear spins in yttrium orthosilicate. The study uses control of the surrounding spin environment as a route to improved coherence in a rare-earth platform.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Treating environmental nuclei as controllable degrees of freedom offers a comparison for spin-bath engineering.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate coherent degrees of freedom of rare-earth centers in solid hosts.

papers.title: Learning unified control of intrinsic nonlinear spin dynamics in atomic qudits for magnetometry
papers.authors: C.-Z. Cao, J.-Z. Han, M. Xiong, M. Deng, L. Wang, Q. Liu, X. Lv, M. Xue
papers.versionEvidence: Matching title and author list in publisher metadata and arXiv record
papers.summary: A reinforcement-learning protocol controls nonlinear spin dynamics in a multilevel atom to prepare and maintain a squeezed measurement quadrature. Model calculations include state-preparation overhead when estimating the resulting magnetic sensitivity.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Makes the metrological benefit depend on both state preparation and the subsequent readout dynamics.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use control sequences to counter evolution that degrades a desired quantum signal.

papers.title: Double-quantum-enhanced coherent control and magnetic sensing of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride
papers.authors: Shihao Ru, Abdullah Rasmita, Jiakai Chen, Yuzhe Yang, Xiaodan Lyu, Robert Cernansky, Edwin Hang Tong Teo, Jesús Zúñiga-Pérez, Fedor Jelezko, Weibo Gao
papers.versionEvidence: Matching title and author list in publisher metadata and arXiv record
papers.summary: Simultaneously driving two transitions of boron vacancies in hexagonal boron nitride enables double-quantum control. Compared under identical conditions, the resulting protocol improves alternating-field magnetometry and supplies a differential test of electric-field and strain noise models.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Directly compares sensing protocols while holding the experimental platform fixed.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use measurement-channel design to improve spin-based sensing.

papers.title: Sensitivity threshold defines the optimal spin subset for ensemble quantum sensing
papers.authors: Suwan I. Kang, Minhyeok Kim, Sanghyo Park, Heonsik Lee, Keunyoung Lee, Donggyu Kim
papers.versionEvidence: Matching title and author list in publisher metadata and arXiv record
papers.summary: An analytical threshold selects the most useful spins from an inhomogeneous ensemble. The study compares the resulting sensitivity with conventional choices and uses phase-only holography to implement the selected illumination pattern while assessing optical nonuniformity.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Shows why including every available spin can reduce the usefulness of an ensemble measurement.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how the composition of a measurement channel influences its sensitivity.

papers.title: Improving the Dynamic Range of Interacting Quantum Sensors via Optimized Quantum Control
papers.authors: Yasuhiro Aota, Yuichiro Mori, Takahiko Satoh, Yuichiro Matsuzaki, Hideaki Kawaguchi
papers.summary: Numerical optimization shapes global control fields so an interacting spin ensemble has a monotonic response over a wider field interval. Adding a variance penalty reduces estimation uncertainty at the expense of some dynamic range.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Explicitly tests the trade-off between unambiguous field range and measurement uncertainty.

relatedPapers.reason: Both design the sensor response to make the target parameter easier to infer.

papers.title: Electrical Stark Tuning and In Situ Field Sensing of $V_{2}$ Silicon Vacancies in a 4H-SiC a-Plane Lateral pin-Diode
papers.authors: Jannik H. Schwarberg, Fedor D. Hrunski, Maximilian Hollendonner, Wolfgang Knolle, Mathias Rommel, Fabian J. Magerl, Jan F. Dick, Jörg Schulze
papers.summary: Silicon vacancies integrated into a lateral diode retain narrow optical transitions after device processing. Electrical bias tunes individual emitters, and their Stark shifts map local electric fields at low temperature, enabling comparison with device simulations.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Shows how device fabrication and electrical control can be evaluated using the embedded optical spin center itself.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect fabrication and contact design to a functional quantum-material device.

papers.title: Millisecond optical coherence and strong collective coupling in an integrated telecom rare-earth photonic platform
papers.authors: Kah Jen Wo, Pavel A. Dmitriev, Karthik Dasigi, Fumiya Hanamura, Steven Touzard
papers.summary: An erbium-doped crystal bonded to a tunable photonic resonator combines long optical coherence with collective light–matter coupling. The integrated device also stores and retrieves optical phase information through coupling to host nuclear spins at cryogenic temperature.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Connects host selection and device integration with measured optical coherence and memory behavior.

relatedPapers.reason: Both study rare-earth optical interfaces and host-assisted storage of quantum information.

papers.title: Maximizing the Photocatalytic Performance of Covalent Organic Frameworks by Decoupling Charge Separation and Recombination via Guest π-Conjugation
papers.authors: Xueying Li, Jianbin Zhong, Ruoshui Luo, Jesse Velasco, Xiaowen Cui, Zhiguo Wang, Junping Xie, Pingzhi Zhang, Zhihai Liu, Yong Pei, Jiajia Wang, Xianshao Zou, Oleg V. Prezhdo, Wei Li
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Experiments and nonadiabatic simulations compare guest molecules with different conjugation inside a covalent framework. Transient spectroscopy supports differences in early charge transfer, while calculations connect suppressed recombination to structural fluctuations and spatial separation of carriers.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Links guest chemistry to excited-state charge dynamics in a porous electronic material.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how the local electronic environment changes the states and dynamics of a framework.

papers.title: Encapsulation of Nitrogen-Rich Imidazole/Pyrazole in an Indium-Based Metal–Organic Framework for Organic Iodide Adsorption
papers.authors: Ting Li, Qingyan Wei, Tianle Lu, Fangyun Chen, Zilu Chen, Huan-Cheng Hu
papers.summary: Introducing imidazole or pyrazole molecules into an indium framework improves organic iodide capture. The authors associate the uptake with charge-transfer interactions and reactions at the nitrogen-containing guests, linking pore composition to the capture mechanism.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Tests guest modification as a specific way to change pore reactivity.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use local chemical recognition sites within a porous framework.

papers.title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
papers.authors: Zhigao Zhu, Yuanhuai Wang, Hanyu Zhou, Junwen Qi, Yue Yang, Yujun Zhou, Gaofeng Zeng, Qing Xu, Jiansheng Li
papers.summary: Hydrogen bonds restrict torsion in imine-linked chains and promote their assembly into a quasi-two-dimensional framework. The more exposed binding sites facilitate gold uptake and reduction, with calculations connecting structural planarization to the reaction energetics.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Relates interchain assembly to the accessibility of binding sites in a crystalline framework.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how interactions between neighboring units control framework organization.

papers.title: Water-Stable Metal−Organic Framework with a Tuned Pore Microenvironment for Selective Acetylene Separation
papers.authors: Wen Jiang, Ke Zhao, Youran Li, Dongmei Wang
papers.summary: A water-stable framework presents uncoordinated oxygen atoms and aromatic surfaces along its channels. Adsorption measurements and multicomponent breakthrough experiments test preferential acetylene capture, including under humid conditions and repeated separation cycles.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Connects a designed pore environment with separation behavior measured in mixed feeds.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use ligand-defined geometry to tune the behavior of a porous framework.
